conceptZh: 小玩具牛用「牛」字的長橫搔鼻子，癢得打了小噴嚏，身上的黑斑竟彈起又吸回原位。
object: A spotted cartoon toy cow and a solid vermilion 牛 sculpture.
morph: The complete glyph remains rigid and unchanged; the cow rubs its nose against the left tip of the longer lower horizontal stroke.
creativeAngle: 不再把牛頭拉成筆畫，改讓完整字形成為搔癢架；小噴嚏讓黑斑像吸盤彈起，製造清楚又溫和的笑點。
promptEn: Create an 8-second animated toy comedy in a locked, straight-on composition against a light cream background with soft studio lighting. A correctly formed Traditional Chinese 牛 sculpture, saturated solid vermilion, is centered and uncropped at about 70% of frame height with generous margins. Its four strokes are clearly readable: a short upper-left falling stroke, a shorter upper horizontal, a longer lower horizontal, and a central vertical extending above the upper horizontal and below the lower one. Keep this exact glyph rigid throughout. A small rounded cartoon toy cow with rubbery black spots approaches from the lower left during the first 1.2 seconds. From 1.2–2.4 seconds, it gently rubs its nose against the exposed left tip of the longer lower horizontal, keeping its body beside the glyph. Its nose twitches; it pauses with puffed cheeks. At 2.7 seconds, one soft squeaky sneeze makes three black spots spring outward from its flank like tiny suction cups, hovering just beside the cow. The cow looks at its suddenly blank flank in surprise; by 3.5 seconds, the spots pop gently back into their original places. Keep the spots away from the strokes. The cow backs out to the left by 4.4 seconds. Hold the complete glyph alone, perfectly still and unobstructed, from 4.4–8.0 seconds. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, saying exactly 「牛、牛、乳牛」: the first 牛 around 0.4 seconds, the second around 1.5 seconds, and 乳牛 around 5.3 seconds while the finished glyph is clearly visible. Allow natural pauses and stop after the word. Keep the sneeze and suction sounds soft; use no music. Only the single target glyph 牛 appears as on-screen text, with no subtitles, vocabulary lettering, watermark, clutter, or flashing effects. Keep every element visibly animated and toy-like.

conceptZh: 乳牛大廚自信地拋起「牛」字麵糰，麵糰只升高一點，自己卻轉得帽子蓋住眼睛；最後用雙角穩穩托住字。
object: One oversized, vermilion dough sculpture shaped precisely as 牛
morph: The dough already has the correct four-stroke 牛 silhouette. It rises slightly during an attempted pizza toss, then settles upright on the chef cow’s horn tips without changing its stroke structure.
creativeAngle: 改用乳牛大廚拋麵糰的失準笑點：大字幾乎沒動，大廚卻自己轉過頭、帽子遮眼，最後意外用雙角接住。麵糰全程維持正確字形，避免把牛角硬變成筆畫。
promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second stylized 3D animated comedy in one locked, frontal shot. Use a pale butter-yellow background, soft studio lighting, and bright, non-neon colors. The original lead is a rotund cartoon dairy-cow chef with rounded black patches, tiny curved horns, a tall floppy chef hat, and an extravagantly confident grin. The only prop is an oversized dough sculpture in saturated solid vermilion, already shaped precisely as the Traditional Chinese glyph 牛. Give it a matte dough texture and enough firmness to preserve its silhouette.

Keep 牛 centered, upright, fully uncropped, and approximately 70% of frame height with comfortable margins throughout. Its four strokes must be unmistakable: a short upper-left falling stroke meeting the left portion of the shorter upper horizontal, a longer lower horizontal, and a central vertical extending above the upper horizontal and below the lower horizontal. Preserve the standard printed proportions and open spaces. The small chef stands underneath, with its face and costume clear of the strokes.

From 0.0–1.3 seconds, the chef balances the enormous glyph on its raised hooves and gives a smug little eyebrow wiggle, preparing a spectacular pizza toss. From 1.3–2.1 seconds, it crouches and flings the dough with tremendous confidence—but the massive glyph rises only a tiny distance, remaining upright. The chef’s effort instead sends its own round body through one quick pirouette underneath. At 2.1–3.2 seconds, its tall hat flops over its eyes. It freezes with empty hooves extended, expecting a catch; the descending glyph gently settles across its two horn tips, supported beneath the long lower horizontal. Leave the central vertical clearly visible between the horns. A soft doughy plop punctuates the surprise. From 3.2–4.5 seconds, the chef lifts the hat brim, looks up at its accidental success, and gives a small sheepish grin. No additional props or decorative flour particles.

From 4.5–8.0 seconds, hold the complete glyph perfectly still and unobstructed. The chef remains motionless beneath it, framing rather than overlapping its silhouette.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, saying exactly 「牛、牛、乳牛」. Place the first 牛 around 0.3 seconds, the second around 1.1 seconds, and 乳牛 around 5.3 seconds during the clear final hold. Allow natural pauses and stop after the word. Keep the spin swish and soft plop quiet; use no music. Only the single glyph 牛 appears as on-screen text. Include no subtitles, vocabulary lettering, logos, watermarks, clutter, or flashing effects.
